clue.text: Speak in public close to hellish ancient river

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so only the end is kept

parts.note: the last letter of hellish
ancient means very old
the Forth is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: An orator holds an audience near some infernal river of antiquity, like the Styx.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forth is the river flowing into the Firth of Forth past Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold forth is an idiom for talking at length, typically lecturing a listening group.

clue.text: Polish bottom of tray, love

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen or polish

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of tray

explanation.surface: Someone polishing the underside of a tea tray, addressing a partner affectionately.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish looks like the nationality, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey is a common term of endearment, used like darling or sweetheart.

clue.text: Flickering light initially surrounding island disappears

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of light

indicators.note: something that disappears is removed from the word it was in

parts.note: ambient means surrounding, as in ambient noise
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A light, seen at first around an island, flickers and vanishes from view.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrounding works as an adjective here, describing atmosphere or background, not as a verb wrapping round something.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes a flame or light that plays softly over a surface, glowing and flickering.

clue.text: Odd characters in fourth century shared bit of tittle-tattle in bed

indicators.note: the odd characters are those in first, third and fifth place

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of fourth
a century is a ton, a hundred; its T is shared with the piece before, so only the rest is added
a T, plentiful in tittle-tattle, is the letter both pieces share

explanation.surface: Odd snippets of fourth-century gossip shared while lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: FUT and TON overlap on their common T rather than simply joining, so the T is written once.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style padded mattress used as a bed, often on a low frame.

clue.text: Ruddy large number to correct

parts.note: ruddy means reddish
a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: A flushed crowd of people set about putting something right.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraft a document is to rewrite it, revising and amending its errors.

clue.text: Rush, record-breaking British goalscorer, picked up in storm

indicators.note: picked up as in heard on a radio, so the words are judged by ear

parts.note: rush means hurry
Harry Kane, England's all-time record goalscorer

explanation.surface: A goal-hungry striker charges forward in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Kane is the England footballer who broke the national scoring record; HURRY KANE said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurricane is a violent tropical cyclone, the most severe category of windstorm.

clue.text: Short note about letter for communicating

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the letters run the other way
something short is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: A flat is a musical note

explanation.surface: A brief memo about a letter that is meant to be sent.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat loses its T and the remaining four letters are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfa is the NATO phonetic alphabet's word for A, used by radio operators when spelling things out.

clue.text: Unfair to lose top mechanic

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: partisan means biased, unfair

explanation.surface: It is unjust that a mechanic should lose his job as head of the workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTISAN loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, and a mechanic in the old sense is exactly that.

clue.text: Untied swimmer in European country

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: France, the European country
an eel is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: A swimmer free of ties to any club competing somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Untied here means not bound to one employer; swimmer is a standard way to clue a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works independently, not tied to any single employer by contract.

clue.text: Also, I reproduced Dutch shed as a cartoon

indicators.note: to shed something is to cast it off, so a letter is lost

parts.note: also means and
D is the abbreviation for Dutch
taken as written
mated means bred, reproduced

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they bred too, then a Dutch garden shed appears in a cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed looks like a garden building but is a verb: AND sheds its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated describes a film or drawing brought to life through cartoon techniques.

clue.text: Quite right, dad, France lost

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so its letter is taken away

parts.note: dad is a father
F is the international code for France

explanation.surface: A father agrees after his French holiday plans fell through.
explanation.walkthrough: FATHER loses the F for France.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather and quite are both mild intensifiers meaning fairly or somewhat.

clue.text: Winged creature very lost in Western Norway

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
letters that are lost have wandered off course and come back in a muddled order

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for western
taken as written
N is the international code for Norway

explanation.surface: A winged beast wanders hopelessly astray among western Norway's fjords.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a heraldic dragon-like beast with two legs and wings.

clue.text: A cat slid around in cream of tartar, perhaps

indicators.note: letters moved around are put into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cat skids about in a bowl of cream of tartar in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Cream of tartar is potassium hydrogen tartrate, a baking ingredient; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid salt keeps a replaceable hydrogen, and cream of tartar is a classic example from baking.

clue.text: Greek meets German in cave

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greek
Otto is a typical German name
joins the two parts

explanation.surface: A Greek and a German have a rendezvous in a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave, natural or artificial.

clue.text: Range of humankind observed in crowd disturbance

indicators.note: something observed in a place is seen inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a riot is a disturbance by a crowd
flesh, as in all flesh, means humankind

explanation.surface: The whole spectrum of humanity seen during a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Range is a distance, not a variety: within rifle shot means within firing range.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle shot as a measure is the distance a rifle bullet carries, its effective range.

clue.text: Welcoming work, meander around

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: letters moved around are put into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A friendly job: wander about at leisure.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-armed describes a warm reception, greeting someone as if with an embrace.

clue.text: Exercise tiring when starting late

indicators.note: starting points to the front of the word as the place where one letter is exchanged for another

parts.note: tiring work is draining
T is time, which says when
late means dead, abbreviated D

explanation.surface: Physical training is exhausting when you get going late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAINING starts with D, late; time swaps in for it at the start. Late meaning deceased, abbreviated D, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is a programme of physical exercise, or one session of it.

clue.text: Rich European takes the place of American that smells?

indicators.note: one thing taking another's place means one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: affluent means wealthy
E is the abbreviation for European
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A wealthy European replaces a smelly American.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: effluent need not smell, but often does.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluent is liquid waste or sewage, which typically gives off a foul odour.

clue.text: Design Immelmann turns, protecting reputedly suicidal individual

indicators.note: to turn is to face the other way, so the text is read backwards
the words protect the solution by holding it inside them

parts.note: read backwards, the letters run across both words

explanation.surface: An aerobatic pilot plans Immelmann turns while guarding a doomed creature.
explanation.walkthrough: An Immelmann turn is an aerobatic manoeuvre, so 'turns' reads as a noun; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemmings are rodents popularly but wrongly believed to commit mass suicide by leaping off cliffs.

clue.text: Son more sick, with temperature, raises support

indicators.note: in a down entry raising means lifting the letters so they read bottom to top

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
iller means sicker
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A son, getting sicker and running a temperature, is propped up.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework that supports climbing plants.

clue.text: Repulsed supporter restraining rowing instructor making missile

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the letters run backwards
something restrained is held inside

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
the cox steers and directs a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A disgusted fan restrains a rowing coach who is building a missile.
explanation.walkthrough: Repulsed looks like disgusted but means driven back. A tee is the peg that supports a golf ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exocet is a French-built anti-ship missile, famous from the Falklands War.

clue.text: Ring coach in Austria to procure musical instrument

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
a coach is a railway car
taken as written
A is the international code for Austria

explanation.surface: Someone phones a coach in Austria to buy a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring looks like a phone call but gives a round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: Repeatedly tame rowdy colleague

indicators.note: rowdy suggests disorderly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the word written twice

explanation.surface: Someone keeps trying to calm down a boisterous co-worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A teammate is a fellow member of a team, a colleague working alongside you.

clue.text: Insufficient silver in pool

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pool
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Not enough silver has been found in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scant or lacking in quantity, not enough.

clue.text: Film instant before contest

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
to vie is to compete, contest

explanation.surface: A quick film made just before a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: Instant looks like an adjective but is a noun here; contest is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Movie is the everyday word for a motion picture.

clue.text: Make-up of scoundrel beginning to get depressed

indicators.note: pushed down, the letter sinks lower in this down entry and settles inside

parts.note: a rogue is a scoundrel

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of get

explanation.surface: A villain's cosmetics start to bring them down.
explanation.walkthrough: The G in ROGUE is pushed down one place, so it sits below the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is a red cosmetic powder or cream applied to the cheeks.

clue.text: Conviction hits me badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone sentenced in court feels the verdict as a heavy blow.
explanation.walkthrough: Conviction reads as a court verdict; it means a firm belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god, a religious conviction.

clue.text: Celebrate despot, mostly wicked, suffering reversal

indicators.note: a reversal turns the order back to front
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Vladimir Putin, Russia's autocratic leader
wicked means evil

explanation.surface: People cheer as a wicked tyrant suffers a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: To live it up is an idiom for partying and enjoying oneself lavishly.

clue.text: Male's platform cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the end is chopped off

parts.note: a stage is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A man's speaking platform gets trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, and loosely a man on his own, as in a stag party.

clue.text: Even with having long time to replace leader in industry, is forlorn

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means one letter is swapped for the others

parts.note: even with means despite
an era is a long period of time

indicators.note: 'leader in' keeps only the first letter of 'industry'

parts.note: first letter of industry

explanation.surface: Even after a long spell running an industry, the boss feels hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: DESPITE swaps its I for ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate means without hope, which is what forlorn conveys.
